title: MATCHA
subtitle: The Whole Story of the Whisked Leaf — History, Craft, Science, and 60+ Recipes
author: Tang Shiuan Jenn
target: comprehensive reference + recipe book; ~140,000 words (~500-600 Kindle pages); reflowable EPUB with an illustration in every chapter

build_days.day1: architecture, art pipeline, cover, Part I + recipe-format chapters (ch22-23)
build_days.day2: Part II (craft) + Part III (science, strictest honesty)
build_days.day3: Part V drinks (41 recipes across ch24-31)
build_days.day4: Part VI bakes (26 recipes) + Parts IV & VII + full QA + EPUB

honesty_policy: No invented studies, statistics, or citations. Health chapters state only well-established general knowledge (caffeine content ranges, L-theanine, catechins/EGCG exist in green tea) in plain language, and say plainly what is uncertain.
No disease-treatment claims, no weight-loss promises, no 'detox'.
The matcha-vs-coffee chapter is a fair comparison, not a hit piece: it says who might prefer each and why, and admits taste is personal.
Recipes are written from sound culinary ratios and say 'ovens and brands vary — taste and adjust'. No 'guaranteed' results.
Commercial chapters describe the boom qualitatively and with widely known public facts; no revenue figures we cannot verify.
All artwork is original. No photographs unless the author supplies her own.
style_rules: Warm, clear, unhurried voice — a knowledgeable friend at a tea counter, never a lecture.
Every chapter opens with a small scene or image in words, then earns its information.
Recipes: intro paragraph (why this one is worth making), ingredient list with metric + US cups, numbered steps, 'the tricky part' note, one variation.
Chinese/Japanese terms given with kanji/hanzi on first use (抹茶, 茶筅, 薄茶, 濃茶) then romanized after.
No products, no URLs, no self-promotion inside the book — it stands alone.
